terms.definition: Any number that can be represented on the number line, including rational and irrational numbers.
A number that can be written as a ratio of integers with a nonzero denominator.
A real number that cannot be written as a ratio of integers.
A whole number, its opposite, or zero.
A rule such as the commutative, associative, distributive, identity, or inverse property used to justify equivalent steps.
A mathematical phrase made from numbers, variables, and operations without an equality or inequality sign.
Having the same mathematical value or meaning even when written in a different form.
A measurable amount described by a number and, when appropriate, a unit.
A standard amount used to describe a measurement.
The level of detail or exactness used to report a measurement or numerical result.
How close a measured or calculated value is to an accepted or true value.
The absolute difference between an experimental and accepted value divided by the accepted value, expressed as a percent.
A reasonable approximate value used to anticipate or check a result.
A judgment about whether a mathematical result makes sense in relation to magnitude, units, context, and prior information.
A specific example that shows a universal mathematical claim is false.
Checking a result independently, such as by substitution, estimation, inverse operations, units, or another valid method.
